title: Training Optimal Large Diffusion Language Models
claim: Diffusion models follow a distinct compute-optimal frontier favoring smaller models and more data than autoregressive ones, and existing models sit off it.
layout: 1 log-log plot with legend on right, optimal-vs-actual annotations with horizontal guide lines
description: A single log-log scatter and line plot. The x-axis is FLOPs (10^17 to 10^25) and the y-axis is parameters (10M to 1T). Four diagonal lines show scaling-law predictions: black and grey dashed lines for Chinchilla Approaches 1 and 2 (autoregressive), and bold red and pink solid lines for Quokka Approaches 1 and 2 (diffusion). The Quokka lines sit below the Chinchilla lines, so they favor fewer parameters at the same compute. Pastel dots mark open-source autoregressive models (Llama 2, Llama 3, Qwen 2, Qwen 3), most of which lie below the Chinchilla lines. A black star marks LLaDA 8B at about 10^23 FLOPs. Red text gives the optimal point (15B model, 1.2T tokens). Black text gives LLaDA (8B model, 2.3T tokens). Thin horizontal lines link these labels to the frontier. The legend sits on the right, grouped into Scaling Laws and Opensource Models. The red lines and the star draw the eye first.
caption: Overlaid predictions from Chinchilla and Quokka (compute-constrained). We overlay the predictions from our approach 1 and 2, along with those from [ref]. Though scaling at the same pace, DLMs are 2--5$\times$ more data-hungry than AR models at the same FLOPs—favor smaller models and larger corpora. We mark the position of LLaDA [ref] in the same space, finding that it's severely over-trained with 2$\times$ smaller models and 2$\times$ more corpora against the Quokka efficient frontier. Meanwhile, wo show the positions of opensource models, finding that most models are over-trained compared with the Chinchilla efficient frontier, except some models from the Llama family. Note that the token statistics are based on the numbers in their reports, which might not be strictly unique tokens. More discussions are detailed in \S [ref].
abstract: We introduce Quokka, the first systematic scaling law for diffusion language models (DLMs), encompassing both compute-constrained and data-constrained regimes, and studying the key modeling and optimization designs. Quokka is a good friend of Chinchilla and provides wider scopes. We hope the results would bring short-term practical guidance in DLMs training and long-term inspirations for the whole AI community.
